search_terms: cells lacking RB1 hyperdependent Aurora B kinase survival
inclusion_rationale: CRISPR synthetic-lethal screen in an RB1-null SCLC line with conditional RB1 re-expression showed RB1-null cells are hyperdependent on AURKB; an Aurora B inhibitor was efficacious in multiple RB1-deficient SCLC preclinical models.

search_terms: Aurora A kinase inhibition synthetic lethal RB1 tumor suppressor
inclusion_rationale: Cell-panel profiling of 36 cell-cycle inhibitors across RB1-mutant vs RB1-wildtype lines identified AURKA inhibition as the strongest RB1-mutation-associated cytotoxicity; AURKA-selective LY3295668 caused durable regression of RB1-deficient xenografts.

search_terms: Aurora A kinase inhibition synthetic lethal RB1 tumor suppressor
inclusion_rationale: In the same RB1-mutant vs RB1-wildtype cell-panel screen, AURKB inhibitors were among the two target classes with the strongest RB1-mutation-selective cytotoxicity.

Chemical and genetic vulnerability screens in an RB1-isogenic lung cancer pair showed AURKA inhibition is synthetic lethal in RB1-deficient lung cancer via stathmin-mediated microtubule destabilization and mitotic death.
Synthetic lethality between RB1 loss-of-function and Aurora kinase A inhibition was tested in RB1-deficient retinoblastoma cells and confirmed in an RB1-deficient xenograft mouse model.

Differential-viability compound screen in retinoblastoma cells found AURKA inhibitors synthetically lethal specifically with RB1 deficiency plus MYCN amplification, validated in zebrafish and PDX models.
High-throughput drug screening in isogenic RB1-biallelic-loss vs RB1-intact hepatocellular carcinoma models showed selective sensitivity to AURKA inhibition, confirmed in vitro and in vivo.

Isogenic RB1-biallelic-loss vs RB1-intact HCC drug screen identified PLK1 inhibitors as selectively lethal to RB1-deficient cells, with synthetic-lethal interactions demonstrated in vitro and in vivo.
Same isogenic RB1-biallelic HCC screen reported selective sensitivity of RB1-deficient cells to KSP/KIF11 (kinesin spindle protein) inhibitors among mitotic-regulator agents.
Isogenic RB1-biallelic-loss HCC models were selectively sensitive to PARP inhibitors, and mitotic+PARP inhibitor combinations were synergistic in vivo.

search_terms: Targeting the vulnerability of RB tumor suppressor loss in triple-negative breast cancer
inclusion_rationale: Drug screens counter-screened in isogenic TNBC lines and panels of varying endogenous RB status identified CHK1 inhibitors as RB-loss-selective; RB-selective efficacy of CHK inhibition was confirmed in xenografts.

search_terms: Targeting the vulnerability of RB tumor suppressor loss in triple-negative breast cancer
inclusion_rationale: The same isogenic/RB-status-stratified TNBC screen identified PLK1 inhibitors as RB-synthetic-lethal, and RB-deficient clinical TNBC specimens expressed high PLK1.

Unbiased drug screen in RB-deficient vs RB-proficient TNBC models showed RB loss creates an enhanced pro-apoptotic vulnerability; the XIAP antagonist birinapant, combined with CHK1 or AURKA inhibitors, gave RB-selective killing and durable in vivo control.

Rb1-deficient breast cancer cells and PDX models were selectively killed by ATR (RP-3500) plus PKMYT1 coinhibition while Rb1-proficient models resisted; Rb1 knockdown sensitized and Rb1 re-expression protected.

Same study: PKMYT1 inhibition (RP-6306) with ATR inhibition induced synthetic lethality specific to Rb1-deficient breast cancer, confirmed by Rb1 knockdown/re-expression and Rb1-deficient vs Rb1-proficient PDX regression.

CRISPR knockout screen showed RB1 loss in TNBC/HGSC generates a synthetic lethal dependency on casein kinase 2 for surviving replication-perturbing agents; CK2 inhibition selectively prevented regrowth of RB1-deficient patient HGSC organoids.

Skp2 deletion completely blocked SCLC formation in Rb1-knockout mice (an Rb1-genotype-dependent effect), and small-molecule SKP2 inhibitors had antitumor activity in RB1-deficient mouse tumors and SCLC PDX models.
In CDK4/6i-resistant ER+ breast models, RB1 loss caused mitotic segregation errors and conferred enhanced sensitivity to TTK inhibition with CFI-402257 relative to RB1-intact models.

search_terms: RB1 loss BCL2 BCL-xL navitoclax dependency
inclusion_rationale: Across xenograft-derived 3D prostate cancer models and cell lines, tumors with RB1 loss were selectively sensitive to BCL-XL inhibition, and navitoclax combinations caused prolonged regression in RB1-loss models.

RB1 loss/E2F activation upregulated ACSL4 and sensitized prostate cancer cells to ferroptosis; the selective GPX4 inhibitor JKE-1674 blocked RB1-deficient tumor growth and metastasis in xenografts and GEMMs.

Genome-wide CRISPR screen in isogenic ER+ RB1-knockout vs parental breast cancer cells identified PRMT5 as an RB1-loss-selective vulnerability; pemrametostat plus fulvestrant inhibited RB-deficient CDX and PDX growth.

E2F1 chromatin binding in Rb-deficient castration-resistant prostate cancer was LSD1/KDM1A-dependent, and Rb inactivation sensitized CRPC tumors to LSD1 inhibitor treatment relative to Rb-intact models.

Across 26 metastatic prostate cancer models stratified by RB1 status, RB1 deficiency and/or replication stress conferred sensitivity and complete regression to a B7H3(CD276)-targeted PBD antibody-drug conjugate, whereas RB1-WT response was governed by SLFN11/DNA-repair status.

Prostate cancer cells with combined TP53/RB1 loss were resistant to all single agents tested but were selectively vulnerable to combined PARP and ATR inhibition, reflecting replication stress from RB1/TP53 loss.
Same study: ATR inhibition combined with PARP inhibition produced significant responses selectively in TP53/RB1-deficient prostate tumor cells.

NUDT15 is co-deleted/co-silenced with RB1; NUDT15/RB1 ploidy score correlated with mercaptopurine sensitivity across 543 cancer cell lines and NUDT15 knockdown sensitized cells to mercaptopurine — a collateral-lethality vulnerability of RB1-deleted tumors.

search_terms: RB1 mutant bladder cancer synthetic lethal target
inclusion_rationale: Computational prediction followed by experimental testing showed selective sensitivity to aryl hydrocarbon receptor inhibition in RB1-mutant versus RB1-wild-type bladder cancer cells.

INVERSE-DIRECTION: In isogenic mantle cell lymphoma clones with RB1 gene knockout versus RB1-intact controls, loss of RB1 conferred resistance to the CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib (CDKN2A deletion and CDK4/MYC overexpression did not).
INVERSE-DIRECTION: Same isogenic RB1-knockout MCL panel — RB1 loss conferred resistance to palbociclib, which inhibits CDK6 as well as CDK4; the sensitive genotype is RB1-proficient.

INVERSE-DIRECTION: Systematic CDK/cyclin dependency mapping across RB-proficient and RB-deficient cancer models showed RB-deficient models are intrinsically CDK4/6-independent, i.e. RB1 loss confers resistance to FDA-approved CDK4/6 inhibitors, with reciprocal cyclin E dependence.
